EPIC_CLASS: class:architectural

## Context
Agents running design-review, ui-designer, brainstorm, preplanning, and sprint workflows currently operate without a shared corpus of UI/UX design knowledge. Each session starts without government-specific anti-patterns, USWDS component guidance, WCAG 2.2 compliance patterns, or established design principles, causing inconsistent and incomplete guidance. This epic establishes the foundational reference library — schema, corpus structure, full initial content, retrieval infrastructure, and source provenance tracking — that five subsequent epics will integrate into specific agent workflows. It absorbs the government anti-pattern catalog from epic 17de-a47a, seeds the full corpus from permissively licensed and Nava-internal sources, and establishes the retrieval contract (ref-query.sh) that all downstream integration epics depend on.

## Success Criteria
- A corpus directory at plugins/dso/data/ui-reference/ with domain-partitioned Markdown files (each ≤500 lines), YAML frontmatter per entry (id, title, domain[], component[], action[], compliance[], severity, story_type[], coverage, source, license), and three Markdown resolution tiers per entry (### Summary, ### Detail, ### Implementation). A _schema.yaml + check-corpus-schema.sh pre-commit hook enforce tag vocabulary across six dimensions: domain, component, action, compliance, severity, story_type. Domain vocabulary includes gov-benefit-flows. License vocabulary includes internal-nava (content from internal Nava sources committed verbatim; restricted to internal use).
- A _index.yaml manifest committed to the repository (not generated at build time), listing every entry with six-dimension tags, one-liner, file path, coverage tier, source, and license. Full inventory readable without loading any corpus file. Regenerated and recommitted on corpus changes.
- A plugins/dso/scripts/ref-query.sh retrieval script using stdlib Python BM25 (self-contained, no external deps); bm25s used as optional performance accelerator if installed, falls back with stderr notice if not. Flags: --top-n (default 8), --tier=summary|detail|implementation, --session-hash dedup, zero-result stderr signal ([ref-query: no results for query: "..." with filters: ...]), completes within 10 seconds.
- Initial corpus covers the following content domains: (a) Government benefit application form patterns (domain: gov-benefit-flows) — one-question-per-page template and sub-patterns (repeatable items, stacking, looping, people list, someone-else option, I-dont-know option, grouping, optional answer); multi-step task list with linear/non-linear support and conditional logic; review page patterns (inline vs. section editing, accordion for long forms, minimal-submit); validation and error messages (dual-location errors, accessibility copy standards, no bottom-of-page errors, arbitrary-validity anti-pattern); claim/application status page (five most common claimant questions, deadline clarity, contact center alignment); document upload (mobile camera vs. desktop upload vs. third-party SDK trade-offs, vendor lock-in risk, camera onboarding pattern); mobile responsiveness (44px touch targets, 16px minimum font, help text over tooltips, reduce-typing-on-mobile principle); confirmation, e-signature, SSN collection, draft/resume, people composition, rights and responsibilities; paid leave application patterns across state PFML programs; employer dashboard, role-based access control, third-party administrator patterns; (b) Government benefit policy context (domain: gov-benefit-flows) — full SNAP lifecycle (application, interview, verification, eligibility, certification, reporting, recertification, program integrity) with state option variants and unhappy-path client flows; (c) Accessibility patterns (domain: accessibility) — WCAG 2.2 AAA patterns cross-referenced to Section 508/OMB M-24-08; 7-category government accessibility test checklist (content accuracy, content structure, responsiveness, keyboard navigation, screen reader, automated checks, time-based media); note that automated tools catch only 20-60% of issues; axe-core and Pa11y integration patterns; (d) Design principles and heuristics (domain: principles) — Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics, Don Norman's principles, GOV.UK Government Design Principles, 18F UX Guide principles, digital.gov federal requirements, Inclusive Design Principles; (e) Anti-patterns (domain: anti-patterns) — 48 government UI/UX anti-patterns (from 17de-a47a at Detail tier; Implementation stretch); Brignull dark pattern taxonomy; SageSELab AidUI 27-class taxonomy; UX anti-patterns from CA EDD, NJ UI, and USDOL projects (users gaming eligibility questions, recertification deadline failure, state-to-state variation constraints); trauma-informed design anti-patterns (institutional trauma perpetuation, safety/trustworthiness/empowerment/cultural-sensitivity failures); (f) Behavioral and cognitive patterns (domain: patterns) — cognitive load checklists, defensive design checklists, representative entries from principles.design; (g) USWDS component and token guidance (domain: components) — USWDS v3 components and design tokens; react-uswds architectural rationale; USWDS selection decision record; (h) Federal copy and plain language (domain: gov-copy) — USWDS forms copy; GOV.UK error/form patterns and Service Manual writing guidance; VA.gov Content Style Guide (error anatomy, capitalization, punctuation); 18F Plain Language guide; Federal Plain Language Guidelines; CDC reading-level guidance; each entry carries a stable rule ID, prior-art citation, and precedence field; (i) Agentic design patterns (domain: patterns) — multi-level transparency for AI caseworker tools (status indicator, tool call log, data source labels); human-in-the-loop interaction patterns; persistent intervention controls; plain language do/don't pairs for agentic interfaces. Summary + Detail required for all entries; Implementation is stretch.
- Integration test at tests/integration/test-ref-library.sh (REPO_ROOT-based paths): (a) session-timeout query returns entry tagged auth/forms or containing "session timeout" in Summary; (b) --tier=summary output has ### Summary, no ### Implementation; (c) manifest integrity — every _index.yaml entry resolves to a file at its declared path; (d) no corpus file exceeds 500 lines; (e) precision sub-test — three representative queries ("USWDS form validation", "WCAG 2.2 keyboard navigation", "government authentication anti-pattern") each return a top result whose frontmatter tags match a predefined expected-tag mapping; (f) completes within 10 seconds.
- ref-query.sh registered as dso ref-query shim; check-shim-refs.sh does not block downstream skill file references.
- A docs/ui-reference-sources.yaml file at the project root tracks each reference source with fields: name, url, type (github-repo|github-repo-private|confluence-page|confluence-space|google-doc|web-spec|website), access (public|internal-nava), credentials_required (bool), pinned version/commit (where applicable), last-synced date, license, and which corpus domains it populates. Internal sources (Confluence pages, Google Docs, private GitHub repos) are supported first-class. navapbc/benefits-delivery-system is registered as type: github-repo-private, credentials_required: true, access: internal-nava, with a note that it is a rich source of benefits delivery design and implementation context pending credentials provisioning. This is the provenance record for all corpus entries.
- Initial corpus includes federal-style-canon entries for government UI copy editing — covering USWDS forms, GOV.UK error/form patterns and Service Manual writing for user interfaces, VA.gov Content Style Guide (error anatomy, capitalization, punctuation), 18F Plain Language guide, Federal Plain Language Guidelines (Plain Writing Act of 2010), and CDC reading-level guidance. Each entry carries a stable rule ID, a prior-art citation, and a precedence field. Required by depending epic f360-3a5b-b8f3-4f86 (gov-copy-writer sub-agent).

## Closure Checks

All success criteria are verifiable within the closing session (directory/file existence checks, script invocation, test run). No items required routing here via the session-infeasibility check.

## Dependencies
- Epic 17de-a47a: 48 anti-patterns (see ticket 17de-a47a description) copied at implementation start; closed as superseded on this epic's completion. Does not block this epic.
- No new runtime dependencies — stdlib BM25 implementation is self-contained.
- Downstream epics 2-6: Unblocked only after SC3 and SC5 pass. This epic must merge to main before downstream skill files reference plugins/dso/scripts/ref-query.sh (pre-commit referential integrity enforcement).

## Approach
Option A — Markdown files with YAML frontmatter, domain-partitioned under plugins/dso/data/ui-reference/ (e.g., anti-patterns/auth.md, gov-benefit-flows/question-page.md, components/uswds-patterns.md). _index.yaml manifest committed to repo. ref-query.sh (stdlib BM25, optional bm25s accelerator) registered as dso ref-query shim. docs/ui-reference-sources.yaml at project root tracks all source provenance — public and internal. Internal Nava content committed verbatim with license: internal-nava. Only script output enters agent context — corpus files never loaded directly. All five downstream integration epics call .claude/scripts/dso ref-query.

| `plugins/dso/scripts/ref-query.sh` | Story 9fee-6947 (stdlib BM25 path) | Story 40a2-d037 adds bm25s accelerator path | All 5 downstream integration epics via `dso ref-query` shim; integration test cfa6-6c7f | Never retired — downstream epics depend on it permanently |

## Scenario Analysis
- bm25s corpus load time timeout (high, runtime): addressed by SC3 10s target and SC5f timing check
- Tag pre-filter zero matches silently (high, runtime): addressed by SC3 zero-result stderr signal and SC1 vocabulary enforcement
- Missing _index.yaml on fresh checkout (critical, deployment): addressed by SC2 committed-not-generated requirement
- Integration test paths break in worktree sessions (high, deployment): addressed by SC5 REPO_ROOT-based path resolution
- Pre-commit integrity blocks downstream skill refs before merge (high, deployment): addressed by Dependencies merge-ordering note
- shim-exempt not applied to ref-query.sh (medium, deployment): addressed by SC6 shim registration
- YAML vocabulary drift causes silent retrieval gaps (high, configuration): addressed by SC1 schema file and check-corpus-schema.sh
- Internal Confluence source inaccessible in CI (medium, deployment): corpus content committed verbatim to repo; Confluence access not required at runtime or in CI
- Private GitHub repo (BDS) inaccessible without credentials (medium, deployment): addressed by credentials_required flag in ui-reference-sources.yaml; corpus seeding from BDS deferred to a contributor with provisioned access

### Planning Intelligence Log
- Web research (Step 2.6): triggered — novel architectural pattern (BM25 corpus retrieval); re-triggered via gate for design tutorials and GitHub reference material research
- Bright-line conditions fired: novel architectural pattern, unfamiliar dependency (bm25s — resolved to stdlib implementation)
- Scenario analysis (Step 2.75): triggered — 8 of 14 scenarios survived blue team filter
- Practitioner-requested additional cycles: web research re-run 1 time (design tutorials + GitHub reference repos)
- Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0): not triggered — follow-ons created as placeholders at user direction
- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): not triggered
- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): not triggered
- Scale context (Step 0): small scale (default) — static corpus ~200-400 entries at initial seeding, CLI invocation only, no concurrent users, 10s query budget is sufficient
- Re-brainstorm enrichment (2026-05-23): Confluence and GitHub research sub-agents added Nava-internal sources; option (a) verbatim with license: internal-nava; SC4 reorganized by content domain; gov-benefit-flows added to schema vocabulary; SC7 expanded to support internal source types; BDS registered as reference-only; EPIC_CLASS line, Closure Checks section, State Lifecycle table, and scale_context PIL field added per skill template audit.

## Research Findings
Permissively licensed repos identified for corpus seeding: uswds/uswds (CC0), SteveBarnett/Checklists (MIT), benbrignell/principles.design (MIT), JenniKobylskiUX/WCAG-Accessibility-UX-Checklist (MIT), SageSELab/AidUI (MIT). navapbc/wic-participant-recertification-portal (Apache 2.0) identified as highest-value navapbc GitHub source: 10 screen-level docs covering a full user-tested government benefit recertification flow plus 10 ADRs with explicit UX rationale. navapbc/template-application-nextjs ADRs 0003+0004 document USWDS selection rationale and react-uswds trade-offs. navapbc/benefits-delivery-system is private and not accessible with current session credentials; registered as reference-only for future contributor. Nava Confluence Pattern Library (PL space, ~52 pages) is the richest single source: cross-project gov-benefit application form patterns from MA PFML, NJ UI, CA EDD, Vermont MABD, Nebraska IB, Login.gov, Maryland FAMLI, MN Paid Leave — all user-tested. Additional high-value Confluence sources: SNAP Policy Requirements hub (PM3, 17 pages), Accessibility Test Checklist (AAN), Trauma-Informed Design Practice Guide (DOH), Lessons Learned from CA EDD/NJ UI/USDOL (NUI), Agentic Design Patterns for Government Services (NL). Gap confirmed: no existing structured machine-readable government UI/UX reference catalog found — this epic fills a genuine void. Stdlib Python BM25 preferred over hard bm25s dependency at this corpus size; bm25s retained as optional accelerator.
